chapter.v:
As snow
in summer and rain in harvest,So honor is not fitting for a fool. [Lev. 21:5; Is. 7:20; Ezek. 44:20]

Like a
flitting sparrow, like a flying swallow,So a curse without cause shall not alight. [Ezek. 4:1 d Ezek. 4:8, 9 e Lev. 26:25; Lam. 1:20] [Ezek. 5:12]

A whip
for the horse,A bridle for the donkey,And a rod for the fool’s back. [Jer. 40:6; 52:16]

Do not
answer a fool according to his folly,Lest you also be like him. [Jer. 41:1, 2;]

Answer a
fool according to his folly,Lest he be wise in his own eyes.

He who
sends a message by the hand of a foolCuts off his own feet and drinks violence.

Like the
legs of the lame that hang limpIs a proverb in the mouth of fools. [2 Kin. 21:9-11; 2 Chr. 33:9; Jer. 2:10, 11; Ezek.]

Like one
who binds a stone in a slingIs he who gives honor to a fool.

Like a
thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkardIs a proverb in the mouth of fools. [Lam. 4:6; Dan. 9:12; [Amos 3:2]; Matt. 24:21]

The great
God who formed everythingGives the fool his hire and the transgressor his wages.

As a
dog returns to his own vomit,So a fool repeats his folly. [2 Chr. 36:14; [Jer. 7:9-11]; Ezek. 8:5, 6, 16 m Ezek. 11:21 n Ezek. 7:4,]

Do you
see a man wise in his own eyes?There is more hope for a fool than for him. [Jer. 15:2; 21:9; Ezek. 6:12 p Jer. 9:16; [Ezek. 6:8]] [Jer. 43:10, 11; 44:27; Ezek. 5:2;]

The lazy
man says, “There is a lion in the road!A fierce lion is in the streets!” [Lam. 4:11; Ezek. 6:12; 7:8] [Ezek. 21:17 t [Deut. 32:36]; Is. 1:24 u Is. 59:17; Ezek. 36:6; 38:19]

As a
door turns on its hinges,So does the lazy man on his bed. [Lev. 26:31; Neh. 2:17]

The lazy
man buries his hand in the bowl;It wearies him to bring it back to his mouth. [Deut. 28:37; 1 Kin. 9:7; Ps. 79:4; Jer. 24:9; Lam. 2:15 x [Is. 26:9]; Jer. 22:8, 9; 1 Cor. 10:11 y Is. 66:15, 16; Ezek. 5:8; 25:17]

The lazy
man is wiser in his own eyesThan seven men who can answer sensibly. [Lev. 26:26; Ezek.] [Deut. 32:23]

He who
passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his ownIs like one who takes a dog by the ears. [Lev. 26:22; Deut. 32:24; Ezek. Rev. 6:8 c Ezek.]

Like a
madman who throws firebrands, arrows, and death,

Is the
man who deceives his neighbor,And says, “I was only joking!”

Where there
is no wood, the fire goes out;And where there is no talebearer, strife ceases.

As charcoal
is to burning coals, and wood to fire,So is a contentious man to kindle strife.

The words
of a talebearer are like tasty trifles,And they go down into the inmost body.

Fervent lips
with a wicked heartAre like earthenware covered with silver dross.

He who
hates, disguises it with his lips,And lays up deceit within himself;

When he
speaks kindly, do not believe him,For there are seven abominations in his heart;

Though his
hatred is covered by deceit,His wickedness will be revealed before the assembly.

Whoever digs
a pit will fall into it,And he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.

A lying
tongue hates those who are crushed by it,And a flattering mouth works ruin.
